abstract: HLA typing from sequencing data is crucial for studying immune gene families, but high allele similarity challenges existing tools. We present ImmuSeeker, comprehensive software for extracting HLA genotypes, expression, and diversity at gene, one-field, and two-field allele levels, with improved Bayesian zygosity inference and graphical phylogenetic visualization. ImmuSeeker was benchmarked against nine established tools using gold-standard HLA datasets, repeated RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and Isoform Sequencing (Iso-Seq) data, and a longitudinal patient cohort, demonstrating superior accuracy, consistency, and analytical utility. ImmuSeeker provides a scalable, robust framework for comprehensive HLA typing and immune system analyses.

Ethics approval and consent to participate: All data used in this study were collected with IRB approval or written informed consent from participants. The COVID-19 study was approved by the University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center Human Research Protection Office (protocol #20-194). De-identified biospecimens and associated clinical data for the autoimmune disease cohort were obtained from the Accelerated Cure Project (ACP) Repository. These samples and data were collected at 10 major MS centers across the United States under a standardized protocol. All participants provided written informed consent, and collection and banking were conducted with IRB approval at the participating sites. Consent for publication: Not applicable.
